title: CDN Engineer (Akamai)
summary: An engineer who configures and runs our Akamai delivery: caching and edge rules, troubleshooting live traffic, and automating changes so they are safe and repeatable.
job_description: CDN Engineer (Akamai) at Example Ltd, London, hybrid. You will configure Akamai properties (caching rules, cache keys, TTLs, edge logic) for our high-traffic sites, investigate and resolve delivery incidents such as origin errors, cache misses and latency spikes, and automate CDN changes with Terraform and CI/CD pipelines so releases are safe and repeatable. Experience with Akamai Property Manager or a similar CDN, HTTP caching and TLS is required. You will join a weekday on-call rota (one week in six). Salary £70,000 to £85,000.

competencies.name: Edge configuration and caching
competencies.description: Designs caching and edge rules that keep sites fast and correct.
competencies.source: Configure Akamai properties (caching rules, cache keys, TTLs, edge logic).

anchors.1: Describes changing cache settings without explaining the effect on hit rate or freshness.
anchors.3: Explains a caching or edge rule they set, why, and how they checked it worked.
anchors.5: Explains several caching decisions with trade-offs (freshness, hit rate, personalised content), how they tested them and the measured result.

competencies.name: Troubleshooting live traffic
competencies.description: Finds and fixes delivery problems under pressure.
competencies.source: Investigate and resolve delivery incidents such as origin errors, cache misses and latency spikes.

anchors.1: Mentions an incident but not the steps taken or the cause.
anchors.3: Walks through an incident: the signals, the steps to isolate the cause, and the fix.
anchors.5: Walks through a complex incident with clear isolation steps (edge versus origin, logs, headers), the root cause, the fix, and what they changed to prevent it.

competencies.name: Automating CDN changes
competencies.description: Makes CDN changes safe and repeatable with code.
competencies.source: Automate CDN changes with Terraform and CI/CD pipelines.

anchors.1: Makes changes by hand and doesn't describe any review or testing.
anchors.3: Describes managing CDN configuration as code with some review or testing before release.
anchors.5: Describes a full pipeline (configuration as code, review, staging tests, gradual rollout, rollback) and its effect on safety or speed.

questions.text: Tell me about a caching or edge rule you designed for a website or API. What did you decide, and how did you know it worked?
Tell me about a time traffic through a CDN went wrong in production. How did you find the cause, and what did you do?
Imagine your team changes CDN settings by hand and a change recently broke the site. How would you make changes safer?

eligibility.text: Do you have the right to work in the UK for this role?
The role includes a weekday on-call rota, one week in six. Does that work for you?

company_facts:
Location: London, hybrid (2 days a week in the office).
Salary: £70,000 to £85,000.
On-call: weekday rota, one week in six, paid separately.
Team: 6 engineers in the Edge Platform team.
Process: this interview, a 60-minute technical conversation with two engineers, then a meeting with the head of platform. Most people hear back within 5 working days.
